newsitem.title: JAPAN: TSE conducting regular check on Bandai, Sega shares.
newsitem.headline: TSE conducting regular check on Bandai, Sega shares.

text.p: Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Friday it was conducting regular monitoring of share price movements of Bandai Corp and Sega Enterprises Ltd, which on Thursday announced plans to merge in October.

"It is part of the exchange's daily routine to watch share price movements and check reasons even when there isn't a merger or some other event which can affect the shares," a TSE spokesman said. "Bandai and Sega are no exception."
The spokesman said that if suspicions of insider trading or other illegal transactions emerged, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) would be notified.
"However, the TSE does not disclose the findings of its daily investigations or whether it has notified the SESC," he added. "We cannot comment on Bandai or Sega."

On Thursday, before the Sega-Bandai merger was announced, toy maker Bandai's shares rose sharply to close at 2,560, up 200 yen, while videogame producer Sega's shares were off 60 yen at 3,660 yen. Brokers attributed Bandai's rise to media reports of booming sales of one of its toys.

After the market closed, the firms announced plans to merge, with Bandai shareholders to receive 0.76 of a share of Sega for each Bandai share. Bandai was down 30 yen at 2,530 yen at midday on Friday, while Sega was down 200 yen at 3,460.
